lesson.intro: A linear equation in two variables describes a straight line in the $xy$-plane: every point $(x,y)$ that makes the equation true lies on the line, and every point on the line makes it true. The Digital SAT returns to this idea constantly -- it asks you to read a slope, to switch between the two standard ways of writing a line, to build a line from two points or from a point and a direction, and to decide when two lines are parallel or perpendicular. Everything in this topic comes back to one number, the slope.

blocks.title: The two forms you must recognise
blocks.body:
A line can be written in \textbf{slope-intercept form} $y=mx+b$, where $m$ is the slope and $(0,b)$ is the $y$-intercept, or in \textbf{standard form} $Ax+By=C$. Slope-intercept form is the one that tells you everything at a glance, so most SAT work begins by solving for $y$. Standard form is convenient when a question asks for intercepts, because setting $x=0$ or $y=0$ leaves a one-step equation.

Going from $Ax+By=C$ to $y=mx+b$ is always the same two moves: subtract the $x$-term, then divide every term by the coefficient of $y$. Doing that in general gives $y=-\frac{A}{B}x+\frac{C}{B}$, so the slope of $Ax+By=C$ is $-\frac{A}{B}$ -- worth memorising, because it turns many questions into a single line of work.

blocks.title: The facts of this topic
blocks.body:
\textbf{Slope through two points:} $m=\dfrac{y_2-y_1}{x_2-x_1}$.

\textbf{Slope-intercept form:} $y=mx+b$, with $y$-intercept $(0,b)$.

\textbf{Point-slope form:} $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$ for a line of slope $m$ through $(x_1,y_1)$.

\textbf{Standard form:} $Ax+By=C$ has slope $-\dfrac{A}{B}$, $x$-intercept $\left(\dfrac{C}{A},0\right)$ and $y$-intercept $\left(0,\dfrac{C}{B}\right)$.

\textbf{Parallel:} $m_1=m_2$. \qquad \textbf{Perpendicular:} $m_1m_2=-1$, that is $m_2=-\dfrac{1}{m_1}$.

blocks.title: What the slope actually says
blocks.body:
The slope is a rate: $m=\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}$ says that increasing $x$ by $1$ changes $y$ by $m$. That single sentence lets you move along a line without ever finding its equation. If a line has slope $-\frac{5}{3}$ and passes through $(3,4)$, then running $3$ to the right drops you $5$, landing on $(6,-1)$.

It also tells you what the picture looks like before you compute anything: positive slope rises left to right, negative slope falls, slope $0$ is horizontal ($y=b$), and a vertical line $x=a$ has no slope at all. Use this as a sanity check -- an answer with the wrong sign on the slope is visibly wrong.

blocks.title: Building a line from what you are given
blocks.body:
Nearly every ``find the equation'' question hands you one of three packages, and each has a fixed route.

\textbf{A point and a slope.} Substitute the point into $y=mx+b$ and solve for $b$. If the point is already on the $y$-axis, as in $(0,-2)$, then $b$ is handed to you.

\textbf{Two points.} Compute $m$ first, then use either point to find $b$. Using the second point afterwards is a free check.

\textbf{Two intercepts.} Write them as the points $(x_{\text{int}},0)$ and $(0,y_{\text{int}})$ and you are back in the two-point case. Intercepts are points, not loose numbers, and treating them as points prevents most mistakes here.

blocks.title: Parallel and perpendicular
blocks.body:
Two distinct lines are parallel exactly when their slopes are equal; the intercepts must differ, or the two equations describe the same line. Two lines are perpendicular exactly when their slopes multiply to $-1$, which means each slope is the \emph{negative reciprocal} of the other: flip the fraction \emph{and} change the sign. The negative reciprocal of $\frac{3}{4}$ is $-\frac{4}{3}$; of $-\frac{1}{2}$ it is $2$; of $5$ it is $-\frac{1}{5}$.

When a question puts an unknown constant inside a coefficient, as in $kx+6y=12$, express the slope in terms of that constant, $-\frac{k}{6}$ here, and then impose the parallel or perpendicular condition as an equation in $k$.

blocks.title: The three mistakes that cost the most points
blocks.body:
\textbf{1. Half a negative reciprocal.} Turning $\frac{2}{3}$ into $\frac{3}{2}$ (flipped, sign forgotten) or into $-\frac{2}{3}$ (sign changed, not flipped). Both appear as answer choices on purpose. Say the phrase in full every time: flip \emph{and} negate.

\textbf{2. Swapped intercepts.} For $3x+4y=12$ the $x$-intercept is $4$ and the $y$-intercept is $3$. Set $y=0$ for the $x$-intercept -- the variable you set to zero is the one you are \emph{not} looking for.

\textbf{3. Sign errors while rearranging.} Moving $2x$ across the equals sign makes it $-2x$, and dividing by a negative coefficient of $y$ changes the sign of \emph{every} term on the other side. Rewrite the whole line rather than editing it in place.

blocks.title: Working faster on test day
blocks.body:
Convert to $y=mx+b$ first, almost always: once a line is in that form, slope, intercept, graph and comparison questions all become reading exercises.

When the answer choices are equations, do not solve the whole problem -- filter. Find the slope you need and cross out every choice with the wrong one; usually two or three vanish at once, and the survivors are separated by their intercept, which one substitution settles.

On a graph question, read the $y$-intercept off the picture, then count rise over run between two lattice points the line clearly passes through. On the Bluebook app you can also enter a candidate equation in the graphing calculator and see whether it lands on the given points; that is often faster than algebra for a two-point question.

blocks.title: Worked example 1: point and perpendicularity
blocks.body:
\emph{Line $n$ passes through $(-3,5)$ and is perpendicular to the line $y=\frac{3}{4}x+2$. Write the equation of line $n$.}

\textbf{Step 1 -- get the slope.} The given line has slope $\frac{3}{4}$. Flip and negate: line $n$ has slope $-\frac{4}{3}$.

\textbf{Step 2 -- use the point.} Substitute $(-3,5)$ into $y=-\frac{4}{3}x+b$: $5=-\frac{4}{3}(-3)+b=4+b$, so $b=1$.

\textbf{Step 3 -- write and check.} Line $n$ is $y=-\frac{4}{3}x+1$. Check by putting $x=-3$ back in: $-\frac{4}{3}(-3)+1=4+1=5$. \checkmark

The step that breaks most often is the sign in $-\frac{4}{3}(-3)$: a negative slope times a negative $x$ is \emph{positive}. Getting $b=9$ instead of $b=1$ is exactly what that slip produces.

blocks.title: Worked example 2: an unknown coefficient
blocks.body:
\emph{In the $xy$-plane, the line $kx+6y=12$ is perpendicular to the line $2x-3y=5$. Find $k$.}

\textbf{Step 1 -- slopes in terms of the letters.} Using $m=-\frac{A}{B}$: the first line has slope $-\frac{k}{6}$, and the second has slope $-\frac{2}{-3}=\frac{2}{3}$.

\textbf{Step 2 -- impose the condition.} Perpendicular means the product of the slopes is $-1$: $-\frac{k}{6}\cdot\frac{2}{3}=-1$, so $-\frac{2k}{18}=-1$ and $-\frac{k}{9}=-1$.

\textbf{Step 3 -- solve and sanity-check.} $k=9$. Then the first line is $9x+6y=12$ with slope $-\frac{3}{2}$, and $-\frac{3}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{3}=-1$. \checkmark

Notice that no point, graph or intercept was ever needed. A parallel or perpendicular condition is a statement about slopes alone, so translate it into one equation in the unknown constant and solve.

problems.stem: The equation of line $\ell$ in the $xy$-plane is $y=-3x+7$. What is the slope of line $\ell$?
problems.solution: In slope-intercept form $y=mx+b$ the coefficient of $x$ is the slope, so reading the equation is the whole job: $m=-3$. The number $7$ is the $y$-intercept, not the slope.

problems.stem: Line $m$ is given by $y=\frac{1}{2}x-6$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the point where line $m$ crosses the $y$-axis?
problems.solution: A line crosses the $y$-axis where $x=0$, and substituting $x=0$ into $y=mx+b$ leaves $y=b$. Here $b=-6$, so the crossing point is $(0,-6)$.

problems.stem: A line in the $xy$-plane passes through $(0,4)$ and has slope $3$. What is the value of $y$ when $x=5$?
problems.solution: The point $(0,4)$ is the $y$-intercept, so the line is $y=3x+4$ with no extra work. Substituting $x=5$ gives $y=19$.

problems.stem: Which equation is equivalent to $2x+y=8$?
problems.solution: Solving for $y$ means moving the $x$-term to the other side, which changes its sign: $y=-2x+8$. Forgetting that sign change is the most common error on this conversion.

problems.stem: What is the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept of the graph of $3x+4y=12$?
problems.solution: Every point on the $x$-axis has $y=0$, so set $y=0$ and solve. The answer $3$ belongs to the $y$-intercept; swapping the two intercepts is the classic slip here.

problems.stem: What is the slope of the line that passes through the points $(-1,4)$ and $(3,16)$?
problems.solution: Slope is the change in $y$ divided by the change in $x$, taken in the same order for both coordinates: $\frac{16-4}{3-(-1)}=\frac{12}{4}=3$. Subtracting the negative $x$-coordinate is what makes the denominator $4$, not $2$.

problems.stem: Which equation represents a line parallel to the line $y=4x-1$ in the $xy$-plane?
problems.solution: Parallel lines have equal slopes and different $y$-intercepts. Only $y=4x+5$ keeps the slope $4$; the other choices change the slope, which tilts the line instead of shifting it.
steps: Parallel lines share the same slope, here $m=4$.
$y=4x+5$ has slope $4$ and a different intercept.

problems.stem: What is the slope of the line $3x-5y=15$ in the $xy$-plane?
problems.solution: Rewrite as $y=\frac{3}{5}x-3$. Dividing by the negative coefficient $-5$ flips both signs on the right, which is exactly where sign errors appear.

problems.stem: A line in the $xy$-plane has slope $\frac{5}{2}$ and passes through the point $(0,-2)$. Which equation represents the line?
problems.solution: Because the given point has $x=0$, it is the $y$-intercept, so $b=-2$ can be written down immediately and the equation is $y=\frac{5}{2}x-2$.

problems.stem: What is the slope of a line that is perpendicular to the line $2x+3y=9$?
problems.solution: The given line has slope $-\frac{2}{3}$. A perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal: flip to $-\frac{3}{2}$ and change the sign to $\frac{3}{2}$. Flipping without changing the sign is the standard trap.

problems.stem: Which equation represents the line that passes through the points $(1,4)$ and $(3,10)$?
problems.solution: Find the slope first, then use one point to pin down $b$. With $m=3$ and the point $(1,4)$, $4=3(1)+b$ gives $b=1$, so the line is $y=3x+1$.

problems.stem: What is the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept of the graph of $y=\frac{2}{3}x-8$?
problems.solution: Set $y=0$ and solve. Multiplying by the reciprocal $\frac{3}{2}$ is faster than clearing the fraction first: $x=8\cdot\frac{3}{2}=12$.

problems.stem: Which equation is equivalent to $y=-\frac{3}{4}x+2$?
problems.solution: Clear the fraction by multiplying every term by $4$, then collect the variables on one side: $4y=-3x+8$ becomes $3x+4y=8$. The $x$-term arrives on the left as $+3x$, not $-3x$.

problems.stem: The graph of a line in the $xy$-plane is shown above. Which equation represents this line?
problems.figure: \begin{center}\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6.2cm,height=6.2cm,axis lines=middle,xmin=-4,xmax=4,ymin=-5,ymax=5,grid=both,grid style={satline},minor tick num=0,xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$},xlabel style={anchor=west},ylabel style={anchor=south},tick label style={font=\tiny},axis line style={-}]\addplot[very thick,satblue,domain=-2:3]{2*x-1};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.6pt,satnavy] coordinates {(0,-1)};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.6pt,satnavy] coordinates {(2,3)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}\end{center}
problems.solution: The line crosses the $y$-axis at $-1$, so $b=-1$. From $(0,-1)$ to $(2,3)$ the line rises $4$ while running $2$, so $m=2$ and the equation is $y=2x-1$.

problems.stem: Line $k$ is parallel to the line $y=-2x+1$ and passes through the point $(4,7)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept of line $k$?
problems.solution: Parallel means the slope is copied, so line $k$ is $y=-2x+b$. Substituting the point gives $7=-8+b$, so $b=15$.
problems.verify:
b = symbols('b')
result = solve(Eq(7, -2*4 + b), b)[0]

problems.stem: Line $n$ passes through the point $(-3,5)$ and is perpendicular to the line $y=\frac{3}{4}x+2$. Which equation represents line $n$?
problems.solution: Perpendicular to slope $\frac{3}{4}$ means slope $-\frac{4}{3}$. Then $5=-\frac{4}{3}(-3)+b=4+b$, so $b=1$. Substituting a negative $x$ into a negative slope produces a positive product, and losing that is what makes $b=9$ look right.

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the line $kx+6y=12$ is perpendicular to the line $2x-3y=5$. What is the value of $k$?
problems.solution: The two slopes are $-\frac{k}{6}$ and $\frac{2}{3}$, and perpendicular lines have slopes whose product is $-1$. Solving $-\frac{k}{6}\cdot\frac{2}{3}=-1$ gives $k=9$.
problems.verify:
k = symbols('k')
result = solve(Eq(-k/6 * Rational(2,3), -1), k)[0]

problems.stem: The graph of $4x+ky=20$ in the $xy$-plane has the same slope as the graph of $y=-2x+7$. What is the value of $k$?
problems.solution: Writing $4x+ky=20$ as $y=-\frac{4}{k}x+\frac{20}{k}$ shows its slope is $-\frac{4}{k}$. Setting $-\frac{4}{k}=-2$ gives $k=2$.

problems.stem: A line in the $xy$-plane has $x$-intercept $6$ and $y$-intercept $-4$. Which equation represents this line?
problems.solution: The intercepts are the points $(6,0)$ and $(0,-4)$, so the slope is $\frac{-4-0}{0-6}=\frac{2}{3}$ and the line is $y=\frac{2}{3}x-4$. Clearing the fraction gives $2x-3y=12$.
steps: The intercepts are the points $(6,0)$ and $(0,-4)$.

problems.stem: Line $\ell$ passes through the point $(2,-1)$ and is perpendicular to the line that passes through $(0,3)$ and $(4,1)$. What is the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept of line $\ell$?
problems.solution: The line through $(0,3)$ and $(4,1)$ has slope $-\frac{1}{2}$, so $\ell$ has slope $2$ and equation $y=2x-5$. Its $x$-intercept comes from $0=2x-5$, giving $x=\frac{5}{2}$; the value $-5$ is the $y$-intercept, not the $x$-intercept.

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the line $y=mx+b$ passes through the points $(2,7)$ and $(5,16)$. What is the value of $m+b$?
problems.solution: The slope is $\frac{16-7}{5-2}=3$, and $7=3(2)+b$ gives $b=1$, so $m+b=4$. Reversing the slope fraction to $\frac{1}{3}$ is what produces the value $\frac{20}{3}$.
problems.verify:
m, b = symbols('m b')
s = solve([Eq(2*m+b, 7), Eq(5*m+b, 16)], [m, b])
result = s[m] + s[b]

problems.stem: Line $\ell$ has equation $y=\frac{2}{5}x-3$. Line $m$ is perpendicular to line $\ell$ and passes through the point $(4,1)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of the point where line $m$ crosses the $y$-axis?
problems.solution: Line $m$ has slope $-\frac{5}{2}$, the negative reciprocal of $\frac{2}{5}$. Then $1=-\frac{5}{2}(4)+b=-10+b$, so $b=11$.
problems.verify:
b = symbols('b')
result = solve(Eq(1, Rational(-5,2)*4 + b), b)[0]

problems.stem: What is the slope of the line that passes through the points $(-1,4)$ and $(3,-4)$?
problems.solution: Both differences must be taken in the same order: $\frac{-4-4}{3-(-1)}=\frac{-8}{4}=-2$. Subtracting in mixed order flips the sign of the answer.

problems.stem: What is the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept of the graph of $2x-5y=20$ in the $xy$-plane?
problems.solution: Set $x=0$, because every point on the $y$-axis has $x=0$. Then $-5y=20$ and $y=-4$.

problems.stem: Which equation represents a line perpendicular to the line $y=-\frac{1}{2}x+3$?
problems.solution: The negative reciprocal of $-\frac{1}{2}$ is $2$: flip the fraction and change the sign. Choice A only changes the sign, and choice D only flips, so neither is perpendicular.
steps: Its negative reciprocal is $2$, so $y=2x-1$ works.

problems.stem: Which equation is equivalent to $6x-2y=18$?
problems.solution: Isolating $y$ requires dividing by $-2$, which changes the sign of every term on the right: $-2y=-6x+18$ becomes $y=3x-9$.

problems.stem: A line in the $xy$-plane passes through the point $(0,5)$ and has slope $-\frac{3}{4}$. Which equation represents the line?
problems.solution: The point $(0,5)$ is on the $y$-axis, so it is the $y$-intercept and $b=5$. With $m=-\frac{3}{4}$ the equation is $y=-\frac{3}{4}x+5$.

problems.stem: The graph of $y=4x+c$, where $c$ is a constant, passes through the point $(2,3)$. What is the value of $c$?
problems.solution: A point on the graph makes the equation true, so $3=4(2)+c$. Then $c=3-8=-5$; adding instead of subtracting gives the trap value $11$.
problems.verify:
c = symbols('c')
result = solve(Eq(3, 4*2 + c), c)[0]

problems.stem: A line in the $xy$-plane is graphed above. Which of the following is an equation of that line?
problems.figure: \begin{center}\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6.2cm,height=6.2cm,axis lines=middle,xmin=-3,xmax=5,ymin=-4,ymax=5,grid=both,grid style={satline},minor tick num=0,xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$},xlabel style={anchor=west},ylabel style={anchor=south},tick label style={font=\tiny},axis line style={-}]\addplot[very thick,satblue,domain=-1:4]{-1.5*x+3};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.6pt,satnavy] coordinates {(0,3)};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.6pt,satnavy] coordinates {(2,0)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}\end{center}
problems.solution: The line meets the $y$-axis at $3$ and the $x$-axis at $2$, so it falls $3$ units while running $2$ units: $m=-\frac{3}{2}$ and $b=3$.

problems.stem: A line in the $xy$-plane has $x$-intercept $8$ and passes through the point $(2,9)$. What is the $y$-coordinate of its $y$-intercept?
problems.solution: The $x$-intercept is the point $(8,0)$, so the slope is $\frac{9-0}{2-8}=-\frac{3}{2}$. Then $9=-\frac{3}{2}(2)+b=-3+b$, so $b=12$.
problems.verify:
b = symbols('b')
result = solve(Eq(9, Rational(-3,2)*2 + b), b)[0]

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graphs of $2x+3y=12$ and $y=mx-4$ are parallel, where $m$ is a constant. What is the value of $m$?
problems.solution: Parallel graphs have equal slopes, and $2x+3y=12$ rearranges to $y=-\frac{2}{3}x+4$, so $m=-\frac{2}{3}$. The different constant terms guarantee the lines really are distinct.
steps: Parallel lines share the slope, so $m=-\frac{2}{3}$.

problems.stem: Line $\ell$ passes through the point $(-4,2)$ and has slope $\frac{1}{2}$. What is the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept of line $\ell$?
problems.solution: From $2=\frac{1}{2}(-4)+b$ we get $b=4$, so $\ell$ is $y=\frac{1}{2}x+4$. Setting $y=0$ gives $x=-8$; the value $4$ is the $y$-intercept, not the $x$-intercept.

problems.stem: The total cost $C$, in dollars, of a gym membership for $m$ months is given by $C=25m+60$, where $60$ dollars is a one-time joining fee. Which equation gives $m$ in terms of $C$?
problems.solution: Undo the operations in reverse order: subtract the joining fee first, then divide by the monthly rate. Dividing before subtracting produces the choice $m=\frac{C}{25}-60$.

problems.stem: The line that passes through the points $(1,-3)$ and $(k,9)$ has slope $4$, where $k$ is a constant. What is the value of $k$?
problems.solution: The slope condition is $\frac{9-(-3)}{k-1}=4$, so $12=4(k-1)$ and $k=4$. Reading the rise as $9-3=6$ instead of $9-(-3)=12$ is the usual sign slip.

problems.stem: Which equation represents a line perpendicular to the line $4x-6y=15$?
problems.solution: Rearranging gives $y=\frac{2}{3}x-\frac{5}{2}$, so the slope is $\frac{2}{3}$ and a perpendicular line has slope $-\frac{3}{2}$. Choice B keeps the size of the slope and only changes its sign, which is not enough.

problems.stem: The line shown in the $xy$-plane above passes through the two marked points. Which equation represents this line in the form $Ax+By=C$?
problems.figure: \begin{center}\begin{tikzpicture}\begin{axis}[width=6.2cm,height=6.2cm,axis lines=middle,xmin=-2,xmax=5,ymin=-8,ymax=4,grid=both,grid style={satline},minor tick num=0,xlabel={$x$},ylabel={$y$},xlabel style={anchor=west},ylabel style={anchor=south},tick label style={font=\tiny},axis line style={-}]\addplot[very thick,satblue,domain=0:4.5]{2*x-6};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.6pt,satnavy] coordinates {(0,-6)};\addplot[only marks,mark=*,mark size=1.6pt,satnavy] coordinates {(3,0)};\end{axis}\end{tikzpicture}\end{center}
problems.solution: The line passes through $(0,-6)$ and $(3,0)$, so $m=2$ and $y=2x-6$. Moving the $x$-term left gives $-2x+y=-6$, or equivalently $2x-y=6$.
steps: From the graph the line passes through $(0,-6)$ and $(3,0)$.

problems.stem: What is the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept of the graph of $y=-\frac{5}{3}x+10$?
problems.solution: Set $y=0$: $\frac{5}{3}x=10$, so $x=10\cdot\frac{3}{5}=6$. A negative slope with a positive intercept must cross the $x$-axis to the right of the origin, so a positive answer is expected.

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of $ax-4y=12$ is parallel to the line that passes through the points $(1,2)$ and $(5,8)$, where $a$ is a constant. What is the value of $a$?
problems.solution: The two-point slope is $\frac{8-2}{5-1}=\frac{3}{2}$, and $ax-4y=12$ has slope $\frac{a}{4}$. Setting $\frac{a}{4}=\frac{3}{2}$ gives $a=6$; note that dividing by $-4$ makes the slope positive, so a negative $a$ cannot work.
problems.verify:
a = symbols('a')
result = solve(Eq(a/4, Rational(3,2)), a)[0]

problems.stem: Line $m$ is perpendicular to the line $y=\frac{3}{5}x-2$ and passes through the point $(3,4)$. What is the value of $y$ on line $m$ when $x=6$?
problems.solution: Line $m$ has slope $-\frac{5}{3}$. Moving from $x=3$ to $x=6$ is a run of $3$, so $y$ changes by $-\frac{5}{3}\cdot 3=-5$, giving $y=4-5=-1$; no intercept is needed.
steps: From $x=3$ to $x=6$ the run is $3$, so the rise is $-\frac{5}{3}(3)=-5$.

problems.stem: Line $\ell$ passes through the points $(-2,7)$ and $(4,-5)$. Line $m$ is perpendicular to line $\ell$ and passes through the midpoint of the segment joining those two points. Which equation represents line $m$?
problems.solution: The midpoint is $\left(\frac{-2+4}{2},\frac{7+(-5)}{2}\right)=(1,1)$ and line $\ell$ has slope $-2$, so line $m$ has slope $\frac{1}{2}$. Then $1=\frac{1}{2}(1)+b$ gives $b=\frac{1}{2}$.

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of $y=mx+4$ passes through the point at which the graph of $2x+y=16$ crosses the $x$-axis. What is the value of $m$?
problems.solution: The graph of $2x+y=16$ meets the $x$-axis at $(8,0)$. Substituting that point gives $0=8m+4$, so $m=-\frac{1}{2}$; using the $y$-intercept $(0,16)$ by mistake makes the equation unsolvable, which is a useful signal that the wrong intercept was taken.
steps: Set $y=0$ in $2x+y=16$: $x=8$, so the point is $(8,0)$.
problems.verify:
m = symbols('m')
result = solve(Eq(0, m*8 + 4), m)[0]

problems.stem: The graph of a line in the $xy$-plane has slope $-3$ and passes through the points $(a,0)$ and $(0,12)$, where $a$ is a constant. What is the value of $a$?
problems.solution: The slope between the two intercepts is $\frac{12-0}{0-a}=-\frac{12}{a}$. Setting $-\frac{12}{a}=-3$ gives $a=4$, and the positive answer matches a falling line that crosses the $x$-axis to the right of the origin.

problems.stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of $3x+ky=12$ is perpendicular to the graph of $y=\frac{3}{4}x-1$, where $k$ is a constant. What is the value of $k$?
problems.solution: The graph of $3x+ky=12$ has slope $-\frac{3}{k}$, and perpendicularity to slope $\frac{3}{4}$ requires slope $-\frac{4}{3}$. Solving $-\frac{3}{k}=-\frac{4}{3}$ gives $k=\frac{9}{4}$.
problems.verify:
k = symbols('k')
result = solve(Eq(Rational(-3,1)/k, Rational(-4,3)), k)[0]

problems.stem: A technician charges a one-time service fee plus a constant hourly rate. The total charge is $145$ dollars for a $2$-hour job and $280$ dollars for a $5$-hour job. If the total charge $C$, in dollars, is a linear function of the number of hours $h$, what is the one-time service fee, in dollars?
problems.solution: The hourly rate is the slope, $\frac{280-145}{5-2}=45$ dollars per hour, and the service fee is the value of $C$ when $h=0$, that is the $C$-intercept: $145-2(45)=55$. Reporting $45$ answers a different question, the hourly rate.
steps: The one-time fee is the value at $h=0$, namely $55$ dollars.
problems.verify:
b, r = symbols('b r')
s = solve([Eq(2*r+b, 145), Eq(5*r+b, 280)], [b, r])
result = s[b]
